## Proof

We are given the joint density
$$f_{X,Y}(x,y)=ye^{-xy-y},\quad x>0,\;y>0,$$
and zero otherwise. We determine the distribution of $Z=XY$.

### Step 1. Verify normalization

$$\int_0^\infty\!\!\int_0^\infty ye^{-xy-y}\,dx\,dy=\int_0^\infty ye^{-y}\left(\int_0^\infty e^{-xy}\,dx\right)dy=\int_0^\infty ye^{-y}\cdot\frac{1}{y}\,dy=\int_0^\infty e^{-y}\,dy=1.\;\checkmark$$

### Step 2. Compute the CDF of $Z=XY$

For $z>0$,
$$F_Z(z)=P(XY\le z)=\int_0^\infty\int_0^{z/y} ye^{-xy-y}\,dx\,dy.$$

Evaluate the inner integral:
$$\int_0^{z/y} e^{-xy}\,dx=\frac{1}{y}\left(1-e^{-z}\right).$$

Substituting:
$$F_Z(z)=\int_0^\infty ye^{-y}\cdot\frac{1}{y}(1-e^{-z})\,dy=(1-e^{-z})\int_0^\infty e^{-y}\,dy=(1-e^{-z})\cdot 1.$$

Hence
$$F_Z(z)=1-e^{-z},\quad z>0.$$

### Step 3. Identify the distribution

Differentiating gives the density
$$f_Z(z)=\frac{d}{dz}F_Z(z)=e^{-z},\quad z>0,$$
and $f_Z(z)=0$ for $z\le 0$.

This is exactly the density of an **exponential distribution with rate parameter $\lambda=1$**:
$$Z=XY\sim\mathrm{Exp}(1).$$

### Conclusion

The product $XY$ has an exponential distribution with rate $1$ (mean $1$), i.e.
$$\boxed{f_{XY}(z)=e^{-z}\mathbf{1}_{\{z>0\}},\qquad XY\sim\mathrm{Exp}(1).}$$
